answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 90 days before it can bid, and caps each identity at one bid per round. Agents named basalt and onyx face the same rule; a whisper of a new account earns no exemption. An attacker seeking 1,000 bidding identities must immobilize $100,000 for three months. The defense makes mass identity creation costly in capital, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
